precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth. That is the truth in spirit and truth: the keeping of God's commandments.
precepts.point: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. There is one word there I want you to emphasise. Must. There is no other way to do it. You must worship him in spirit and truth, which is the application of God's laws.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Hosea prophesied: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” These are those days. We were out for a long time, without the understanding of who we were as a people or what the will of God was for us, and in the last days the Lord raised up the prophets on the earth again to teach the word of God and apply it, so we could be delivered out of here. Where in the New Testament do we read that the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord? Right here: “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.” That's us, reviving in this time. What you are part of is the resurrection of God's Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign. The Father is going to try us to see if we will worship him according to spirit and truth.

And what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Worshipping in truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Emphasise one word: must. There's no other way to do it. Take one law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We must congregate, it's a holy convocation; we cannot cook, clean, shop, buy or sell on the Lord's Sabbath. There's no deciding it's not important. It's those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. If someone won't congregate with the body and goes to congregate with somebody put out of the body, that's sin: can two walk together except they be agreed? We rationalize in our mind what we think God will be all right with, but his thoughts are not our thoughts. Do what he told you to do.

Where the law is not applied, Hosea says the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” To break out is to break away from the law: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Blood touching blood is violence and hatred against each other. “Therefore shall the land mourn”: if those same sins abide in the body, the congregation won't grow or flourish. So leaders must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example themselves. What God asks is a small thing next to the sins we have committed: not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath holy. The truth is all we've got to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death.

precepts.text: Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold. It's talking about God's word.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” What are the pounds? God's word.

David says: “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” The commandments are more precious than gold, so the money the nobleman hands his servants is his word: the knowledge, the understanding, the faith he bestowed on each of us.

Occupy till I come means do something with it until he returns. When he comes back he wants to know “how much every man had gained by trading”: how much each one went out and taught the word. The servant who laid his pound up in a napkin kept the word to himself, and that is how he is judged.

precepts.text: Thy law is the truth. So now we know the love of God goes back to his laws; of course, his laws in Christ. You can't ignore Christ.
precepts.point: That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness: the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness: sin. All deceit of sin, breaking God's laws. In them that perish, because they received not the love of the truth: this is about our people.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is his law. So now we know what the love of the truth is in 2 Thessalonians 2:10: the love of God goes back to his laws. Of course, his laws in Christ. You can't ignore Christ.

His righteousness is an everlasting righteousness. So when they say God's laws are done away with, that's blasphemy. The white man taught our people that: the Catholic Church first, then the Protestant church picked it up and pushes it worldwide.

So they that perish are the ones who received not the love of his law, the truth, that they might be saved.

precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The proud have digged pits for God's people.

They are not after God's laws. Look at it: how come you can abort in America? How come gay marriage is legalized? They don't keep God's laws and they don't uphold God's laws, but a lot of you coons out there follow behind this white man. They are not after God's commandments.

And who are the proud? Obadiah answers: it is Edom. The man that rules over another in Ecclesiastes 8 is the same proud one digging pits for Jacob, and his own pit is where he is headed.

precepts.text: The truth: thy law is the truth. He is the embodiment of it; he fulfilled and will fulfil all prophecies. Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says he is also “the truth.” The psalm says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and Christ is the embodiment of all these things. He fulfilled, and will fulfil, all the prophecies: he came in the volume of the book, as it was written of him.

So when Christ says, I am the truth, he is saying he is the law of God walking in the flesh. Everything from beginning to end has Christ in it, which is why the Old Testament established everything else, and why we need here a little and there a little to unlock the scriptures. To come to the Father by Christ is to come by the truth, his everlasting righteousness and his law.

precepts.text: Christ said, Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. You see it right there in red.
precepts.point: The wondrous thing out of God's commandments: he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.text: That is what it meant in the Old Testament: Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy. Holiness is us coming into perfection.
precepts.point: The wondrous thing out of God's commandments: he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

precepts.text: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them. Offenses and fear of tribulation will not make you turn your back on Christ.
precepts.point: Peter laid the instructions for marriages in hard times. We see marriage counsels where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor, or a sister wants to give up the faith and go back to the world, or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming where you will be worried about surviving; how much more in a household where husband and wife are striving against each other? Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying, and increasing our faith, following the instructions laid forth.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

precepts.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Paul says, “be not conformed to this world”, because of who rules over this world: the white man. Don't have the mind of the Edomite, the mind of Cain. Instead, “be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, after Christ. Just before, Ephesians told us, “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” That is what we have to do. But how do we really go about doing it?

David asks the same question: “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” How can we cleanse our ways? “by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

The renewing of the mind comes by the word. We have to take heed according to the word, and that is how the bitter spirit, the leaven of Cain and Esau, is cleansed out, so that we may prove “what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:

God's law is the truth, and that is what these religions would have you depart from. We are in the latter times now. Some of you men and women listening will depart from the truth of Christ: some because of persecution for the word's sake, and some because you see signs and wonders, technological signs and wonders, and believe we have been wrong all this time. It is already written, as Christ said: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders”, and “Behold, I have told you before.”

They give heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: they have the Bible, but they are hypocrites. And “having their conscience seared with a hot iron”: you can't wake them up. “Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats”: that is Roman Catholicism, which forbids the men to marry and commands you to abstain from meats during Lent. The religion of the false prophet starts with Christianity.

But the law is the truth, and those who believe and know the truth receive with thanksgiving what God created, and do not depart from his everlasting righteousness.

precepts.text: Thy law is the truth.
precepts.point: Verse 3 says meats are received with thanksgiving by them which believe and know the truth. The truth is the law, so the meat is sanctified by the word, not by a prayer over it.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

precepts.why:

Meats “which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.”

What is the truth? David answers: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is God's laws. Those who know the law receive what God created with thanksgiving; those seduced by doctrines of devils forbid to marry and abstain from meats.

Why do people get seduced into all this crap? Because they were idle, I-D-L-E, and they were given Christianity, an idol, I-D-O-L. Christianity is an idolatrous religion. The one who holds the law, the truth, will not depart from the faith.

A brother knows how to pick up a Glock 17 and how to sell drugs, but cannot stay awake through four chapters a day. The law is the truth, and it is what unshackles the spiritual chains on our brains. Kill that old man with it, or be killed serving him.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The water poured out of his buckets is the word. “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word, as the church is cleansed with the washing of water by the word. That is how you cleanse your spirit: the water is the word, and his seed in many waters is Israel scattered all over the earth.

precepts.text: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord; walking in the way of God is keeping his commandments.
precepts.point: Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days.

note.label: Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated

precepts.why:
“Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.” Walking in the way of God is keeping his commandments.

That is what Moses was given to teach: “Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days”, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left. The undefiled in the way are the ones who walk in the law, and that is the blessing.

precepts.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.” The word is the light: the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and when they speak not according to this word it is because there is no light in them.

So the standard for “that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord” is the word set before us, not personal standards of what feels good in the heart. The word lights the path, and at the end of it is the reward, to go in and possess the good land.

precepts.text: My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.
precepts.point: Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.” That is the Bible defining its own word: righteousness is the commandments.

Moses says the same: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Words like testimony, righteousness, grace and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself, for the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

So when the son asks what the testimonies, statutes and judgments mean, the answer starts with the history, “We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt”, and ends here: all his commandments are righteousness, kept at all times, for our good always.

precepts.text: David prayed, take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; do not let me reach the point where I utter foolishness, hatred, and evil communications.
precepts.point: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth”. When you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. David prayed for exactly that: “And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; for I have hoped in thy judgments.”

Do not let me reach the point where I utter foolishness, hatred, and evil communications. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech. David hoped in the judgments of the Lord, and asked that the word of truth never be taken utterly out of his mouth. That is the first step of the formula for success: the law in your mouth.

precepts.text: A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” A young man cleanses his way by taking heed to it according to the word of the Most High.

That is the circumcision of the heart: no surgery, but repentance, ceasing to do evil and taking heed to your way by the word. The flesh was circumcised at the hill of the foreskins; the mind is circumcised by the word.

precepts.text: The truth is the law: thy law is the truth.
precepts.point: How do we serve the Lord in sincerity and in truth? A lot of people today say they love the Lord, yet they do not do any of his commandments; they do not truly show they have the faith of Christ, because they do not keep the commandments.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

The truth is the law. So worshipping him in spirit and in truth, and serving him “in sincerity and in truth”, means keeping his law. The spirit is his word; the truth is his law. That is how you serve the Lord, and that is what Israel forsook when they said, give us a king.

precepts.text: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments; so David feared after Uzzah.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.”

So David feared after Uzzah. “David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah”, and “David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?” He had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of him and his judgments.

So David would not bring the ark into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. It stayed there three months, “and the Lord blessed Obed–edom, and all his household” because of the ark.

precepts.text: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments.
precepts.point: Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.”

David had felt the judgment of the Most High. He was pardoned, but the child that was born to him surely died, as Nathan said. His repentance was not a light thing; it came from a man afraid of the Lord’s judgments. Out of that repentance Solomon was born, and the Lord loved him.

precepts.text: The righteousness of the Most High is everlasting and his law is the truth, the truth in which David's seed was to walk.
precepts.point: There was a stipulation for the throne to continue: if his children take heed to their way and walk before the Most High in truth with all their heart, the throne stands. Reading through the kings, we see many who broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

David charged Solomon to keep the charge of the Lord his God, “to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. And the throne came with a stipulation: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

The truth David’s seed was to walk in is the law. The righteousness of the Most High is everlasting, and his law is the truth. Reading through the kings, many broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous; the throne stood or fell on whether they walked in that truth.

precepts.text: Before affliction Job strayed, but the chastening turned him back to keep God's word.
precepts.point: He makes sore and binds up; He wounds and His hands make whole. The same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”. This is a heavy truth: correction is a blessing, not a punishment unto death. “Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word.”

Before affliction Job strayed, but the chastening turned him back to keep God's word. The Most High does not chasten us to kill us but to get us better, to show us the way he wants us to go and the instructions we can apply to our lives so we do not keep learning the same lessons over and over. He makes sore and binds up; the same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

precepts.text: It is good to have been afflicted, that one might learn God's statutes.
precepts.point: He makes sore and binds up; He wounds and His hands make whole. The same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why: “It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.” That is why happy is the man whom God corrects. The affliction is good because through it we learn his statutes, the instructions we can apply to our lives so we do not keep learning the same lessons over and over. He wounds, and his hands make whole: the same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals, and the man who learns his statutes from it is happy.

precepts.text: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments; even King David, who taught his hands to war and could leap a wall, feared the Lord.
precepts.point: Wisdom and understanding are hid from all living and given only to the few, the remnant of Israel who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations; we fear the Lord like King David, the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who still trembled at God's judgments.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
“And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.” Job breaks it down: wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and understanding is to depart from evil.

We fear the Lord like King David: “My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” David was the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who taught his hands to war and could leap a wall, and even he trembled at God's judgments. That trembling is the wisdom that is hid from the eyes of all living.

precepts.text: A young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David says the Lord recompensed him “according to the cleanness of my hands”. How do we get clean hands? “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

A young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word. We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism. That is what David means when he says he kept the ways of the Lord and did not put away his statutes from him.

precepts.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? By taking heed thereto according to thy word; that is how we are converted and changed.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” That is how we are converted and changed: by taking heed according to the word.

We cannot change ourselves any more than the Ethiopian can change his skin. The law of the Lord converts the soul, and the young man cleanses his way by taking heed to it.

precepts.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet and a light unto my path; the word enlightens your eyes and becomes a light to navigate life.
precepts.point: The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. When the commandments enlighten your eyes you know where to walk, you will not stumble, you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.” The word enlightens your eyes and becomes a light to navigate life.

With the commandment of the Lord enlightening the eyes, you can see the path, you will not stumble, and you stay focused on keeping God's laws. The word is the lamp to the feet and the light to the path.

precepts.text: The word, the Commandments, is the lamp and light David means in verse 1; the Most High gave us the Commandments as instructions to walk through this captivity.
precepts.point: Even with everything coming against us today, covid-19, the vaccine, all the different things being pushed, wars going on, these words remind us that in this we can be confident. Whether it is other camps, family, or other nations coming against us, we can still be confident.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” The light David means is the word: “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”

The word, the Commandments, is the lamp and the light of verse 1. The Most High is David's guide and his way to salvation, and He gave us the Commandments as instructions to walk through this captivity. It is a rhetorical question: if the Most High is my salvation, why should I be afraid of anybody?

precepts.text: We cleanse our ways by taking heed to the word, meaning the Commandments.
precepts.point: David asks to be washed thoroughly from his iniquity and cleansed from his sin. The question is: how are we going to be washed?

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: David asks, “Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.” The question is: how are we going to be washed? Psalm 119 gives the answer. “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” We cleanse our ways by taking heed to the word, meaning the Commandments. That is the washing David is asking for.

precepts.text: Seek the Most High with the whole heart and ask not to wander from his Commandments; in a world of evil communication we pray that he keep us on the path clean.
precepts.point: David asks to be washed thoroughly from his iniquity and cleansed from his sin. The question is: how are we going to be washed?

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.” Cleansing comes by taking heed to the word, so we seek the Most High with the whole heart and ask him not to let us wander from his Commandments. In a world of evil communication, that is the prayer: that he keep us on the path clean. That is what it is to be washed throughly from iniquity and cleansed from sin.

precepts.text: Thy word is very pure, therefore thy servant loveth it, the mark of a pure-hearted reading of the scriptures.
precepts.point: We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; He put us in captivity for our disobedience. As long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks the Most High to remember how “the foolish man reproacheth thee daily” and to “Forget not the voice of thine enemies: the tumult of those that rise up against thee increaseth continually.” The enemy thinks evil upon their beds every day on how to oppress and crush Israel.

Against that stands the servant of Psalm 119: “Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.” That is the mark of a pure-hearted reading of the scriptures. The foolish man reproaches; the servant loves the word because it is pure.

That is the clean heart we have to come with. He put us in captivity for our disobedience, but as long as we come with a clean heart, loving his pure word and fixing what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting. Let the poor and needy praise his name.

precepts.text: God's laws are the truth; His righteousness is an everlasting righteousness.
precepts.point: His truth shall be our shield and buckler. The shield is what you use to protect yourself, so we have to understand what the truth is.

note.label: Psalm 91: Dwelling in the Secret Place of the Most High

precepts.why:
“He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.” The shield is what you use to protect yourself, so we have to understand what the truth is. Psalm 119 tells us: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's laws are the truth, and his righteousness is an everlasting righteousness. So the shield and buckler that covers whoever dwells in the secret place of the Most High is his law.

When we say the Most High is our refuge and fortress and put our trust in him, he delivers us from the snare of the fowler and the noisome pestilence, and the law is what we hold up as our shield.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness; the commandments are everlasting and are not done away with.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The righteousness he judges with is everlasting, and his law is the truth; the commandments are everlasting and are not done away with.

That is why he can judge the world with righteousness when he comes: the law he judges by has never changed.

precepts.text: The righteousness of the Most High is an everlasting righteousness and His law is the truth.
precepts.point: The Most High is good, His mercy is everlasting, and His truth endures to all generations. That truth is His laws, which endure to all generations.

note.label: Psalm 100: Make a Joyful Noise Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.” That truth is his laws, which endure to all generations.

David says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” His law is the truth, and his righteousness is everlasting, just as his mercy is everlasting.

So the truth that endures to all generations is the law of the Most High. Enter his gates with thanksgiving and bless his name for it.

precepts.text: Departing from the precepts and the judgments of the Most High is sin, as Israel confessed they had done wickedly and rebelled by departing from His precepts.
precepts.point: Once we depart from the precepts we are in the midst of sin. The prayer here is that our ways were directed to keep His statutes, so that we shall not be ashamed when we have respect unto all His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thou hast commanded us to keep thy precepts diligently.” The word precept means law, commandment, rule. That is what a precept is, so precept upon precept is talking about the word of the Most High, the scriptures, the law.

Daniel shows what departing from them is: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”. Israel confessed that they had done wickedly and rebelled, and the rebellion was departing from his precepts.

Once we depart from the precepts we are in the midst of sin. That is why the prayer is “O that my ways were directed to keep thy statutes!”: to keep them diligently and not be ashamed, having respect unto all his commandments. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, because without the law we are defiled.

precepts.text: Now ye are clean through the word which He has spoken; it is the word of the Most High that cleanses us from our sins.
precepts.point: I will meditate in Thy precepts. We have to meditate on the word of the Most High day and night, the same thing said in Joshua 1:8, delighting in His statutes and not forgetting His word.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” Christ says the same: “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.”

It is the word of the Most High that cleanses us from our sins. It cleanses our brains, our mind, cleaning the filth that is within our heart, which is actually the mind. The word hidden in the heart is what keeps a man from sinning against him.

precepts.text: This says the same thing as Psalm 119, that the Most High guides them who keep His commandments and precepts, and that we must not let our sins weigh us down.
precepts.point: I will meditate in Thy precepts. We have to meditate on the word of the Most High day and night, the same thing said in Joshua 1:8, delighting in His statutes and not forgetting His word.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.”

This says the same thing as Psalm 119. The Most High guides them who keep his commandments and precepts, the ones who seek him with the whole heart and pray not to wander from his commandments. And we must not let our sins weigh us down: the young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word, meditating in his precepts and not forgetting his word.

precepts.text: He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, that they should not see nor understand and be converted; the eyes must first be converted before a man can see this truth.
precepts.point: I am a stranger in the earth; hide not Thy commandments from me. Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from Thy commandments. His testimonies are the delight of the servant and his counselors even when princes sit and speak against him.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” Our people's eyes are closed and shut to the truth of this Bible. “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.”

The eyes must first be converted before a man can see this truth. The only way we will see it is if we keep the laws of the Most High; once we keep them our eyes start to open to the truth around us, to who we are, what is required of us, who our enemies are and who the other nations are. But you have to be converted in the laws first.

precepts.text: The law of the Most High is perfect, converting the soul; it is the law that converts us so that our eyes can be opened.
precepts.point: I am a stranger in the earth; hide not Thy commandments from me. Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from Thy commandments. His testimonies are the delight of the servant and his counselors even when princes sit and speak against him.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” It is the law that converts us, so that our eyes can be opened to behold wondrous things out of it.

That is why the prayer is to keep his word and have his eyes opened together: the law converts the soul, and the converted eyes see. His testimonies become the servant's delight and his counsellors, even when princes sit and speak against him.

precepts.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the words spoken are spirit and life, so it is the word that quickens us and changes us.
precepts.point: Behold, I have longed after Thy precepts; quicken me in Thy righteousness. Another word for precept is the law or the rules, and to be quickened means to be changed toward the righteousness of His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have longed after thy precepts: quicken me in thy righteousness.” Another word for precept is the law or the rules, and to be quickened means to be changed toward the righteousness of his commandments.

“It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” The words are spirit and life, so it is the word that quickens us and changes us. Teach me the way of thy statutes, give me understanding, make me to go in the path of thy commandments: the quickening comes through the word.

precepts.text: Fear the Most High and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man, our whole purpose upon this earth.
precepts.point: I will walk at liberty, for I seek Thy precepts. I will speak of Thy testimonies also before kings and will not be ashamed, because we have the wisdom of this Bible, not the wisdom of this world.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever.” Solomon gives the conclusion: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.”

Our whole duty while we are on this earth is to keep the laws of the Most High. It is our whole purpose upon this earth, continually, for ever and ever.

precepts.text: The law has dominion over a man as long as he lives, so as long as we are alive on this earth the law is not done away with.
precepts.point: I will walk at liberty, for I seek Thy precepts. I will speak of Thy testimonies also before kings and will not be ashamed, because we have the wisdom of this Bible, not the wisdom of this world.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?”

As long as we have breath the law has dominion over us; it is not done away with. That is why the psalm says “So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever”, and why we can walk at liberty seeking his precepts and speak of his testimonies before kings and not be ashamed, because we have the wisdom of this Bible, not the wisdom of this world.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.
precepts.point: Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage. A pilgrimage is your walk, your journey in this truth through the straight gate, now learning the laws of the Most High and being reborn again. That walk should be our song, knowing we are the top nation and understanding why we went into slavery and how to come out.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.” Paul says why the word comforts: “whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We get comfort in our afflictions from this Bible, because it is what changes us, and through the patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope. Sometimes we need affliction to get right with the Most High; in their affliction they seek him early, as Hosea 5:15 says. We need to get afflicted sometimes so we can come back to him, and the word is the comfort in it.

precepts.text: We are no more strangers and foreigners, not so-called blacks and Hispanics and native Indians anymore, but fellow citizens with the saints, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ being the chief cornerstone.
precepts.point: Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage. A pilgrimage is your walk, your journey in this truth through the straight gate, now learning the laws of the Most High and being reborn again. That walk should be our song, knowing we are the top nation and understanding why we went into slavery and how to come out.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage.” A pilgrimage is your walk, your journey in this truth through the straight gate, now learning the laws of the Most High and being reborn again.

“Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. We are no more strangers and foreigners, not so-called blacks and Hispanics and native Indians anymore, but fellowcitizens with the saints, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ the chief corner stone.

That walk should be our song: knowing we are the top nation, and understanding why we went into slavery and how to come out.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word it is because there is no light in them, so a man turns his feet back to this Bible to repent.
precepts.point: I am a companion of all them that fear Thee, and of them that keep Thy precepts. You have to be a companion, a friend, to those that keep the laws of the Most High; that is who your companions need to be.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.” Where does a man turn his feet? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

A man turns his feet back to this Bible to repent. If anyone speaks not according to this word, there is no light in them; so the servant makes haste and delays not to keep his commandments, and does not forget his law even when the bands of the wicked have robbed him.

precepts.text: Ye are My friends if ye do whatsoever I command you, meaning follow this Bible.
precepts.point: I am a companion of all them that fear Thee, and of them that keep Thy precepts. You have to be a companion, a friend, to those that keep the laws of the Most High; that is who your companions need to be.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy precepts.” Christ says the same of friendship: “Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.”

Friendship with Christ is following this Bible, doing whatsoever he commands. So you have to be a companion, a friend, to those that keep the laws of the Most High; that is who your companions need to be.

precepts.text: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous; the heart is made sound in wisdom by keeping the laws of the Most High.
precepts.point: Let those that fear Thee turn unto me, and those that have known Thy testimonies. Let my heart be sound in Thy statutes, that I be not ashamed, sound in the wisdom of this Bible among the nations.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Let my heart be sound in thy statutes; that I be not ashamed.” “He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly.”

The heart is made sound in wisdom by keeping the laws of the Most High. He lays up sound wisdom for the righteous, and he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly, so the servant is not ashamed among the nations but sound in the wisdom of this Bible.

precepts.text: Speak thou the things which become sound doctrine, meaning the laws of the Most High, this Bible spoken in wisdom.
precepts.point: Let those that fear Thee turn unto me, and those that have known Thy testimonies. Let my heart be sound in Thy statutes, that I be not ashamed, sound in the wisdom of this Bible among the nations.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine”. Sound doctrine is the laws of the Most High, this Bible spoken in wisdom.

A heart sound in his statutes speaks the things which become sound doctrine. That is how the servant is not ashamed, and how those that fear the Most High are glad when they see him, because he has hoped in his word.

precepts.text: The throne of iniquity frameth mischief by a law and gathers against the soul of the righteous to condemn innocent blood, but the Most High is our defense.
precepts.point: They had almost consumed me upon earth, but I forsook not Thy precepts. Quicken me after Thy lovingkindness, so shall I keep the testimony of Thy mouth. The mischief is framed by law, giving rights to sodomites and signing all kinds of wickedness, but the Most High is our defense.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The pits are traps set by the proud. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law? They gather themselves together against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.”

The throne of iniquity is America, the pinnacle of sin, where once you go out your doors sin is everywhere. It frames mischief by a law, giving rights to sodomites and signing all kinds of wickedness, and gathers against the soul of the righteous to condemn innocent blood. Are you going to have fellowship with that? The answer should be no.

They had almost consumed us upon earth, but the Most High is our defense, and we forsake not his precepts.

precepts.text: Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law till all be fulfilled, which is a future prophecy of all coming into perfection.
precepts.point: I am Thine, save me, for I have sought Thy precepts. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me, but I will consider Thy testimonies. I have seen an end of all perfection, but Thy commandment is exceeding broad.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven.” Christ says the same: “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.”

This word has been here from the beginning and endures for ever; not one jot or tittle passes from the law until heaven and earth pass. “till all be fulfilled” is a future prophecy of all coming into perfection, which is why the psalm says “I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad.”

precepts.text: Days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom, but it is the spirit and the inspiration of the Almighty, keeping and applying the laws of the Most High, that gives understanding; great men are not always wise.
precepts.point: I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep Thy word. I have not departed from Thy judgments, for Thou hast taught me. How sweet are Thy words unto my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth. Through Thy precepts I get understanding, therefore I hate every false way.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.” Job says how that can be: “I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom. But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.”

You would expect the aged to have the wisdom, but it is the spirit and the inspiration of the Almighty, keeping and applying the laws of the Most High, that gives understanding. “Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.”

So through his commandments a man is made wiser than his enemies and understands more than the ancients. The law has to be our meditation all the day; through his precepts we get understanding, and therefore we hate every false way.

precepts.text: Thou shalt discontinue from thine heritage and serve thine enemies; our heritage and testimonies were taken away and we were made to serve our enemies, taught that the Most High is white and loves everybody, when the testimony is that He is black and Christ is black and died for the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians.
precepts.point: The wicked have laid a snare for me, yet I erred not from Thy precepts. Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever, for they are the rejoicing of my heart. I have inclined mine heart to perform Thy statutes alway, even unto the end.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart.” Jeremiah shows what happened to that heritage: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

Our heritage and testimonies were taken away, and we were made to serve our enemies in a land we knew not. There we were taught that the Most High is white and loves everybody, when the testimony is that he is black and Christ is black and died for the so-called blacks, Hispanics and native Indians.

Taking his testimonies back as an heritage for ever, and inclining the heart to perform his statutes even unto the end, is taking back what we discontinued from.

precepts.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High, which is the Bible, shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty, which is the protection.
precepts.point: Thou hast trodden down all them that err from Thy statutes, for their deceit is falsehood. Those that err from this Bible, their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way. My flesh trembleth for fear of Thee, and I am afraid of Thy judgments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word.” The hiding place is protection. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.”

The secret place of the Most High is the Bible. He that dwells in it abides under the shadow of the Almighty, which is the protection: hold thou me up, and I shall be safe.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do His commandments, so if you keep them you should not be afraid but fear the one true Power.
precepts.point: Thou hast trodden down all them that err from Thy statutes, for their deceit is falsehood. Those that err from this Bible, their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way. My flesh trembleth for fear of Thee, and I am afraid of Thy judgments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. So if you keep them you should not be afraid of the evildoers or of them that err from his statutes, but fear the one true Power. He has trodden down all them that err from his statutes, for their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way.

precepts.text: Thou art My servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified; the servant of this Bible is the Israelites, the ones who will get the understanding and the testimonies.
precepts.point: Therefore I love Thy commandments above gold, yea, above fine gold. Therefore I esteem all Thy precepts concerning all things to be right, and I hate every false way. You have to esteem all the laws of the Most High above everything and hate every falsehood.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.” Isaiah names the servant: “Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”

The servant of this Bible is the Israelites. They are the ones who will get the understanding and the testimonies, who love his commandments above fine gold, esteem all his precepts concerning all things to be right and hate every false way. It is time for the Most High to work, for they have made void his law, and he will be glorified in his servant Israel.

precepts.text: Let all things be done decently and in order, according to the word.
precepts.point: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, so the Israelites are to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness. Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not Thy law.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.” “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

All things must be done decently and in order according to the scriptures, according to the word. So when a law or order comes out that agrees with this Bible, we must abide in it; that is our steps ordered in his word, so that no iniquity has dominion over us.

precepts.text: A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, the wisdom of knowing the interpretation of a thing.
precepts.point: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, so the Israelites are to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness. Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not Thy law.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; and teach me thy statutes.” “Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.”

A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, the wisdom of knowing the interpretation of a thing. When the Most High teaches his servant his statutes, that wisdom is what makes the face shine.

precepts.text: The law endures for ever, and Jacob is told to walk in the presence of the light of the commandments that he may be illuminated; the Israelites are the ones to be illuminated to shine upon this earth.
precepts.point: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, so the Israelites are to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness. Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not Thy law.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.”

The law endures for ever, and Jacob is told to take hold of it and walk in the presence of its light that he may be illuminated. The Israelites are the ones to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, to shine upon this earth: letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness.

That is the face made to shine, and the entrance of his words that giveth light and understanding unto the simple, the same as verse 105, where the word is the lamp and the light.

precepts.text: Sanctify them through Thy truth; Thy word is truth.
precepts.point: The laws of the Most High are everlasting and are the truth, the truth of who we are and what will set us free.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Christ prays the same: “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The laws of the Most High are everlasting and are the truth, and we are sanctified through it. The word is pure, undefiled, and it is the truth of who we are and what will set us free.

precepts.text: There is no peace, saith the Most High, unto the wicked.
precepts.point: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies, yet do I not decline from Thy testimonies. Thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of Thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“There is no peace, saith the Lord, unto the wicked.” That is why “Salvation is far from the wicked: for they seek not thy statutes.” Salvation is very far from them because they have no rest in their wicked ways and no peace, and it does not matter whether it is the wicked among our people or the wicked among the nations.

David stands on the other side of that: “Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law. Plead my cause, and deliver me: quicken me according to thy word.” The one who does not forget the law can ask to be quickened; the wicked who seek not the statutes have no peace to look for.

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
precepts.point: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies, yet do I not decline from Thy testimonies. Thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of Thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.” This is the reason salvation is far from the wicked: evil pursues them. They have no rest in their wicked ways and no peace, and it is the same for the wicked of our people and the wicked of the nations.

But to the righteous good shall be repaid. David has many persecutors and enemies, yet he does not decline from the testimonies; he beholds the transgressors and is grieved because they kept not the word. So he can say, “Great are thy tender mercies, O Lord: quicken me according to thy judgments.”

precepts.text: In the beginning was the Word; this word was here before anything.
precepts.point: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies, yet do I not decline from Thy testimonies. Thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of Thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” David says “Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.” This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

That is why David loves the precepts and will not decline from the testimonies no matter how many his persecutors are: the word he holds to was here from the beginning, and its righteous judgments endure for ever.

precepts.text: Blessed is he whosoever shall not be offended in Christ, that is, not offended with every word in this Bible, since the Bible represents Christ.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” David says “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Not being offended in Christ means not being offended with every word in this Bible, since the Bible represents Christ.

Princes persecuted David without a cause, yet his heart stood in awe of the word; he rejoiced at the word as one that findeth great spoil, and he hated and abhorred lying, all the falsehood and backbiting against us, while loving the law. Sometimes we do get offended, but that is part of our pilgrimage.

precepts.text: We are told to return to the Most High, forsake our sins, and offend less in the things we are battling.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins, make thy prayer before his face, and offend less.” Great peace have they which love the law and nothing shall offend them, but sometimes we do get offended, and that is part of our pilgrimage. So we are told to return to the Most High, forsake our sins, and offend less in the things we are battling.

Repentance is a two part step: confessing and forsaking. It is done with counsel, seeking it from leadership rather than covering our sins.

precepts.text: I die daily; a man must die daily and offend less in the things he is dealing with.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
Paul says “I die daily.” A man must die daily and offend less in the things he is dealing with. Sometimes we do get offended, but that is part of our pilgrimage, and dying daily is how we come to the great peace of them that love the law, whom nothing shall offend.

That is the same walk David describes: “Lord, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments.”

precepts.text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper, but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy, so repentance is confessing and forsaking, with counsel.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” Repentance is confessing and forsaking, with counsel; we seek counsel from leadership rather than covering our sins.

That is how we offend less in the things we are battling, part of our pilgrimage toward the great peace of them that love the law. David lived that way: “My soul hath kept thy testimonies; and I love them exceedingly. I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my ways are before thee.” Nothing was covered; all his ways were before the Most High.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; the lost sheep are the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Let my soul live, and it shall praise Thee, and let Thy judgments help me. I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant, for I do not forget Thy commandments. The lost sheep is the house of Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early and follow this Bible, fleeing the strange doctrines.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” The lost sheep are the house of Israel. So when David says “I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments”, that is Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early.

That is who this whole cry belongs to: “Let my cry come near before thee, O Lord: give me understanding according to thy word.”

precepts.text: My sheep hear My voice and follow Me; we follow this Bible, and a stranger will they not follow but flee from him, leaving the strange doctrines alone.
precepts.point: Let my soul live, and it shall praise Thee, and let Thy judgments help me. I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant, for I do not forget Thy commandments. The lost sheep is the house of Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early and follow this Bible, fleeing the strange doctrines.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:” The lost sheep of the house of Israel hear his voice and follow him, and we follow this Bible. A stranger they will not follow but will flee from him, so we leave the strange doctrines alone.

That is the sheep David describes: gone astray, yet “I do not forget thy commandments”, longing for salvation, with the law as his delight and his tongue speaking of the word, “for all thy commandments are righteousness.”

precepts.text: Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage forever; the testimonies of who we are and who Christ came for.
precepts.point: These are the curses we are under. Our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings and from our homeland.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why: “Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart.” The testimonies are a heritage too: the testimonies of who we are and who Christ came for. Children are an heritage of the Lord, and so is his word to them.

precepts.text: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.
precepts.point: For thou shalt eat the labor of thine hands. There is profit in laboring, and this is not just the nine to five, it is laboring in this truth. We have too many people in IUIC who just talk and do not labor at all, and shame on you. You will escape this world by your works.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.” Walking in his ways is walking in God’s commandments: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.” When we walk in the laws of the Lord we are undefiled; when we do not, we are defiled.

precepts.text: His law is the truth, so we must worship Him according to the commandments.
precepts.point: He is near to all who call upon Him in truth. Calling upon Him in truth means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” His law is the truth, so calling upon him in truth means keeping his commandments; we must worship him according to the commandments. He is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works, and he is nigh to those who call on him that way.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
David tells what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is named in the psalm as the law itself.

So “grace and truth came by Jesus Christ” does not put the law away. Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator. The law is the truth, and the truth came by Jesus Christ with grace, through that mediator, instead of a man's own blood.

precepts.text: His righteousness is everlasting and his law is the truth, so to walk in truth is to keep his commandments.
precepts.point: To fear him and work righteousness means to keep the commandments; "devout" means to keep the law of the Most High.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
To fear him and work righteousness means to keep the commandments. “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

His law is the truth and his righteousness is the law. So “he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness” is the man who keeps his commandments.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: The ten pounds. Pounds is money; this is money. What is it going into? “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” So these pounds represent something so precious, which is the word of God, the commandments.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: What does it mean, I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire? “The law of thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver.” See that: the law of thy mouth, that is talking about the Bible, is better than gold. That is talking about the scriptures. This is the gold that has been tried in the fire, because he said my word shall never fail.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Anoint thine eyes with eyesalve. What does eyesalve do? Like when Visine gets the red out: Christ wants us to see clearly what the word of God is saying. “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” So when we send up our prayers we have to ask God to give us understanding, open our eyes to what the word of God is saying, because many of these scriptures have two and three meanings. God, open my eyes so that I can see. That is why he said anoint thine eyes with eyesalve.
